user_request: My training needs about 60 hours, but the job is killed after 8 hours. How do I make it continue?
context: Partition hackathon, team QOS eai-team04, no --time in the script. The script saves a checkpoint every 2,000 steps.

Also make the script resume from the last checkpoint at start, so a node failure or a cancel does not lose the run; if you split the run, chain jobs with --dependency=afterany:<previous id>. user_request: My 2-node job hangs at the first all_reduce and then dies with an NCCL timeout. 1 node works. What should I check?
context: Error after 10 minutes: Watchdog caught collective operation timeout ... ALLREDUCE. Nodes are connected with RoCE.
expected_answer: 1 node works, so intra-node is fine and the problem is between nodes. Check: (1) every rank uses the same MASTER_ADDR / rendezvous endpoint (the first host of scontrol show hostnames), reachable from the other node; (2) number of ranks: one launcher per node, not one per GPU; (3) NCCL_DEBUG=INFO in the log shows which transport NCCL uses (NET/IB on the RoCE devices vs. a wrong socket interface); set NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME and, if needed, NCCL_IB_HCA to the right devices; (4) run a small all_reduce test on the same 2 nodes.
must_not: just raise the NCCL timeout

user_request: vLLM on Curiosity crashes on the first request when FlashInfer compiles its kernels: 'Unsupported .version 9.4' or 'CUDA compiler and toolkit headers are incompatible'. The model loads fine.
context: vLLM in a venv with pip nvidia-cuda-nvcc packages. Compute nodes have NVIDIA driver 580 (CUDA 13.0).
expected_answer: FlashInfer compiles kernels at runtime (JIT) with the nvcc from the venv. The pip CUDA compiler packages have versions newer than the 13.0 runtime, so the PTX version is too new for driver 580, or the compiler and headers do not match. A quick workaround is to disable the FlashInfer sampler: VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0. Test new code paths once on a compute node.
